Editor-in-Chief
*Obstetrics & Gynecology*
American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists

Dear Editor,

We are pleased to submit our original research manuscript, "Access to Generalist Obstetrics and
Gynecology Care at Private Equity-Backed vs. Independent Practices: A Mystery Caller Audit
Study," for consideration for publication in *Obstetrics & Gynecology*.

Private equity ownership of outpatient physician practices has expanded rapidly over the past
decade, including within obstetrics and gynecology, and a growing literature links private
equity ownership in health care to higher costs and mixed-to-worse quality across settings
[@borsa2023systematic; @bruch2020hospital; @kannan2023adverse]. Audit ("secret shopper") studies
have separately shown that Medicaid enrollees face higher appointment-denial rates and longer
waits than commercially insured patients across specialties [@bisgaier2011auditing;
@asplin2005insurance]. To our knowledge, no prior study has examined whether the ownership
structure of generalist OB-GYN practices, specifically corporate private equity ownership versus
independent practice, shapes access and scheduling disparities by insurance type. We addressed
this gap with a mystery-caller crossover audit of matched private equity-backed and independent
clinics, pre-registering two hypotheses before any call was placed: that private equity-backed
clinics decline new Medicaid patients more often than matched independent practices, and that
among practices that do schedule Medicaid patients, the wait-time gap between public and
commercial insurance is wider at private equity-backed clinics.

The manuscript reports a matched-pair design across 26 U.S. states, a pre-specified statistical
analysis plan frozen before fielding (including seven pre-specified sensitivity analyses), and a
STROBE-compliant reporting checklist submitted alongside this letter. We believe the findings are
of direct relevance to *Obstetrics & Gynecology*'s readership and to the intensifying federal and
state scrutiny of health-care consolidation's effect on access to reproductive health care.

This manuscript is original, has not been published previously, and is not under consideration
elsewhere. All authors have reviewed and approved the submission and have no conflicts of
interest to disclose. The study protocol was reviewed by the Colorado Multiple Institutional
Review Board (COMIRB). [Protocol status is stated as "exempt" in the study repository but as
"approved ... with a waiver of consent" in an earlier manuscript draft; this discrepancy must be
resolved against the real COMIRB determination letter, and the exact wording of this paragraph
corrected accordingly, before this letter is sent.]

Thank you for your consideration. We look forward to your response.

Sincerely,

Tyler Muffly, MD
Corresponding author, on behalf of all authors
